The Grailed $120 commission cliff, worked through

Since 20 May 2026, Grailed's commission is 6% on a sale under $120 (minimum $1.99) and 9% on a sale of $120 or more, plus 3.49% + $0.49 payment processing on a domestic sale. The tier is a step. At $120 the 9% rate applies to the whole sale, so some higher prices pay you less than a lower one. The figures below are the same arithmetic the Grailed fee calculator runs; the rates come from third-party fee guides, so check one real payout.

Five domestic sales, no buyer-paid shipping

Item priceCommissionProcessingYou keepEffective rate
$20.00$1.99 (minimum)$1.19$16.8215.9%
$50.00$3.00 (6%)$2.24$44.7710.5%
$100.00$6.00 (6%)$3.98$90.0210.0%
$119.99$7.20 (6%)$4.68$108.119.9%
$120.00$10.80 (9%)$4.68$104.5212.9%
$200.00$18.00 (9%)$7.47$174.5312.7%

Raising the price by one cent, from $119.99 to $120.00, cuts what you keep by $3.59. The dead zone runs from $120.00 to about $124.09; a price of $124.10 is the first that nets what $119.99 does ($108.11).

What it changes if you collect shipping

Shipping the buyer pays you on your own label is added to the sale before the tier is chosen, so the cliff sits that much lower in item-price terms. With $12 of buyer-paid shipping, an item at $108 puts the sale at $120 and the 9% rate applies to all $120; the same $3.59 drop applies, and the break-even price is $112.10. With a Grailed label the buyer's shipping goes to the carrier, so only the item price counts and the cliff stays at $120.

Compared with the old flat 9%

Until 20 May 2026 every sale paid 9%. A $50 item then kept $43.27 and now keeps $44.77, so cheaper items got cheaper to sell. At $200 the old and new schedules agree at $174.53. Many articles and fee calculators still show only the flat 9%, which overstates the fee under $120.

Do this with your own sale

The Grailed fee calculator runs this on your own item price, shipping, label and cost, solves for the price that hits a target profit (below the cliff when that is cheaper), and shows the old flat 9% and an international buyer side by side. Nothing you type leaves your browser. Want Grailed ranked against other channels for the same piece? Open the where-to-sell calculator, or see the Depop, Poshmark and Mercari calculators.

Common questions

How much does Grailed take on a $100 sale?

A 6% commission ($6.00) plus 3.49% + $0.49 processing ($3.98), so a domestic seller keeps $90.02 -- a 10.0% effective rate. There is no listing fee, subscription or buyer fee.

What is the Grailed $120 commission cliff?

At $120 the commission jumps from 6% to 9% on the whole sale, not just the part above $120. A $119.99 sale pays you $108.11 and a $120.00 sale pays $104.52, so you must list at about $124.10 to net what $119.99 does. Prices from $120.00 to $124.09 all pay less than $119.99.

Should I price a Grailed item at $119 instead of $120?

If you were going to land between $120 and about $124, yes: $119 keeps more than any price in that band. Above about $124.10 the higher price wins again. The calculator shows both sides for your own shipping and label cost.

Does the $1.99 minimum commission matter?

Only on small sales. 6% is less than $1.99 until the sale reaches $33.17, so a $20 sale pays $1.99 (about 10% of the sale) instead of $1.20, and the effective rate on a $20 item is 15.9% once processing is added.

      Common questions

      How much does Grailed take per sale?

      Two fees, nothing else. A commission of 6% on sales under $120 (minimum $1.99) or 9% on sales of $120 and over, plus payment processing of 3.49% + $0.49 on a domestic sale. On a $100 sale that is $6.00 + $3.98, so you keep $90.02. There is no listing fee, subscription or buyer fee.

      Why does a $120 sale pay less than a $119.99 sale?

      Because the commission tier is a step, not a slope: at $120 the 9% rate applies to the whole sale, not just the part above $120. A $119.99 sale keeps $108.11 while a $120.00 sale keeps $104.52, and you need to list at about $124.10 to net the same as $119.99. Pricing just under $120, or well clear of it, avoids the dead zone.

      Is Grailed still a flat 9% commission?

      Not since 20 May 2026, according to the fee guides this tool is built from: sales under $120 moved to 6% (with a $1.99 minimum) and sales of $120 and over stayed at 9%. Many older articles and fee calculators still show a flat 9%, which overstates the fee on cheaper items.

      Does the commission include shipping?

      It includes shipping the buyer pays you directly (your own label). With a Grailed-provided label the buyer's shipping goes to the carrier, so the commission is on the item price alone. Enter buyer-paid shipping only if you collect it yourself; the amount is added to the sale before the tier and the processing fee are worked out.

      No. Arithmetic happens entirely in your browser. Item prices, costs, and payouts are never uploaded. vs-tracking-grailed-sales-in-a-spreadshe.text:
← Grailed fee calculator

Grailed Fee Calculator vs. tracking Grailed sales in a spreadsheet

Most Grailed sellers who price more than a handful of pieces end up with a spreadsheet: a column for the commission, one for processing, one for what the piece cost. Since the commission became a 6% / 9% step on 20 May 2026, the formula is no longer a single multiplication, and a copied "Grailed takes 9%" cell quietly overstates the fee on everything under $120.

What each approach actually does

A spreadsheet can reproduce every rate this calculator applies: 6% under $120 with a $1.99 minimum, 9% from $120, and 3.49% + $0.49 processing. It needs a tier formula, a minimum, and a rule for whether buyer-paid shipping counts. It also means keeping the rates current when Grailed changes them.

This calculator has the tiers built in, shows the payout drop at $120, and solves backwards for the price that hits a target profit on the correct side of that step. It compares the current schedule with an international buyer and the old flat 9% for the same piece in one click.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?No. Everything runs in your browser; your figures stay on this device.

Common questions

Can a spreadsheet do this math instead?

Yes. The 6% and 9% commission tiers, the $1.99 minimum and the 3.49% + $0.49 processing fee are each ordinary arithmetic. Building it means a nested IF for the tier, a MAX for the minimum, and a separate formula to back into a target-profit price.

What does a spreadsheet not do that this calculator does?

Solve backwards across the $120 step. Because payout drops at $120, the price that hits a target profit can be below it or above it, and a single rearranged formula gets one side wrong. The calculator solves each tier and picks the lowest valid price, and it shows the dead zone for your shipping setup.

Is a spreadsheet ever the better choice?

Yes, when your situation has a wrinkle this calculator does not model, such as a bundle in one sale, a promotional credit, or a fee change since the rates here were last checked. A spreadsheet you update yourself can represent any rule you can describe.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The calculator runs entirely in your browser. Item prices, costs, and payouts are never uploaded, and the optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day, never your numbers.
